clue.text: New stand-it may be reserved

indicators.note: new tells us to make something fresh out of these letters, a new arrangement of them

explanation.surface: A fresh stand might be booked in advance for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reserved' looks like 'booked', but here it means aloof. 'New' rearranges STANDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved person is cool and remote in manner, which is the distant sense of the word.

clue.text: Put out of action-ails-bed is called for

indicators.note: a rearrangement is called for, so the letters of the fodder must be put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone ill is ordered to bed and put out of action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is called for' asks for the letters AILSBED to be reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: To disable something is to stop it working, to make it useless.

clue.text: Being the leading player, Edward began

parts.note: the star of a show is its leading player
Ted is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Edward got his start as the lead actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Started is a simple synonym of commenced, the past tense of start.

clue.text: She's against dividing money up

indicators.note: dividing means the letter goes into the middle and splits the other piece
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: the lira was the currency of Italy
V is short for versus, meaning against

explanation.surface: A woman who opposes splitting the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LIRA into ARIL, and V goes inside it. The 's after 'She' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Avril is a girl's name, so it can stand for a female person.

clue.text: Announcer once involving Crown in row

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another, here inside the word for a row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

indicators.note: involving suggests tangling up, so the letters of the word Crown are mixed

explanation.surface: An old herald gets mixed up in a dispute with the monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' signals a tangle of the Crown's letters; 'in' then puts them inside. 'row' looks like a quarrel but is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A town crier was an official who walked the streets calling out public news, a historic herald.

clue.text: Totally lacking in aspiration?

parts.note: read as having no aim or goal at all, an aim also being called an end, so the word is literally without one

explanation.surface: Someone with no ambition at all.
explanation.walkthrough: An end is an aim, so having none at all, 'less' an end, describes something that goes on for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without an end, whether a goal or a stopping point, is everlasting.

clue.text: A woman trains all individually

parts.note: Eve, the first woman in Genesis, is the stock crossword woman
RY is an abbreviation for railway, the thing trains run on

explanation.surface: A coach puts each member of the squad through training.
explanation.definitionFit: Every means each one of a group, taken one by one.

clue.text: The dunderhead is proceeding to make a speech

parts.note: the head of the word dunder is its first letter
taken as written
a course is a way of proceeding, a line of action

explanation.surface: A fool is about to address an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dunderhead' looks like a fool but means the head, first letter, of 'dunder'.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourse is to talk at length on a subject, to lecture.

clue.text: Looks at a metal container, finding it an ugly thing

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
ore is rock that contains metal

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a tin can and finds it unsightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metal container' suggests a tin or can, but ore is the rock that holds metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is a thing unpleasant to look at, such as a hideous building.

clue.text: Given direction, tot set out, though most unhappy

parts.note: S is south, a compass direction
to tot up is to add

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of the word set are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A small child, told what to do, is put outside and is very sad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a child but is the verb to add up. 'out' rearranges SET into EST.
explanation.definitionFit: Saddest is the superlative of sad, the most sorrowful.

clue.text: A bird and salmon swallowed by a pig

indicators.note: swallowed by means taken inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
a parr is a young salmon

explanation.surface: A pig gulps down a bird and a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparrow is a small brown songbird, a common garden species.

clue.text: A journalist has to tote a gun in this part of London

indicators.note: to tote is to carry, so the journalist holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist
the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: A reporter must carry a weapon in a rough area of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tote' means carry, so the editor holds the gun. The East End is the traditionally working-class area of east London.
explanation.definitionFit: The East End is a district of London east of the City.

clue.text: Yell at the contest

parts.note: read as a cry raised at a fight, a contest being a struggle or combat

explanation.surface: A spectator shouts at a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: The contest is a fight, and the yell is the shout raised as troops charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle cry is the shout of soldiers going into combat, or a rallying slogan.

clue.text: Ring the sector supplying the gas

parts.note: the letter O is round, like a ring
a zone is a sector or area

explanation.surface: Phone the area supplying the gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call but is the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is a form of oxygen, a pungent gas found high in the atmosphere.

clue.text: Duck is always about the same

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for always goes around the other piece

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always
id. is short for idem, Latin for the same

explanation.surface: A duck never changes.
explanation.walkthrough: E'ER (always) goes 'about' ID, short for idem, Latin for 'the same'.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a large sea duck prized for its soft down.

clue.text: Sorry about imprisoned social worker

parts.note: re means about or concerning
pent, as in pent up, means shut in
the ant is a social insect, and a worker ant is a kind of ant

explanation.surface: An apology over a jailed welfare officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' suggests a welfare officer, but means an ant, a social insect of the worker caste.
explanation.definitionFit: A repentant person is regretful and contrite for a wrong done.

clue.text: Tense, and that's not good

definitions.meaning: a verb tense expressing continuous past action in grammar
flawed or faulty, falling short of perfection

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious, which is a bad thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective, nervous, but it is the grammar noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The grammatical tense for incomplete past action shares its name with the word for flawed, having defects.

clue.text: Quickly getting a job as the orderly

parts.note: a post is a job or position

indicators.note: orderly means put into order, so the letters are rearranged into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Someone lands a job as a hospital attendant fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orderly' looks like a hospital attendant but rearranges ASTHE into HASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste means with great speed, as fast as possible.

clue.text: Silly saps without the game needed by travellers abroad

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece goes around the other
silly suggests the letters of the word saps are muddled up

parts.note: a sport is a game

explanation.surface: Foolish people who skip the match need documents for going overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' reorders SAPS into PASS, which goes 'without' (outside) SPORT. 'without' looks like 'lacking' but is the old sense 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: Passports are travel documents that people must carry to cross international borders.

clue.text: The way a boy goes around a ship

indicators.note: goes around means the first piece surrounds the others

parts.note: a page is a boy servant
SS is short for steamship

explanation.surface: A lad walks round a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a way through, a corridor or route.

clue.text: What a guy's called is certain to hold him back

indicators.note: to hold means one piece contains the other

parts.note: sure means certain

indicators.note: back means the word is read the other way round

parts.note: him refers back to the guy, a man

explanation.surface: A person's name is bound to keep him back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'him' points back to the guy, a man; 'back' reverses that word before 'to hold' puts it inside the word for certain.
explanation.definitionFit: A surname is the family name by which a person is known.

clue.text: … but here's someone who never wanted to go abroad

definitions.text: … but here's someone who never wanted to go abroad

parts.words: … but here's someone who never wanted to go abroad
parts.note: following the travellers of the previous clue, this person was sent overseas against their will, banished

explanation.surface: Unlike the travellers with documents, this person left the country unwillingly.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to the previous clue about travellers needing passports.
explanation.definitionFit: An exile is someone banished from their homeland, forced to live abroad.

clue.text: Copy some would like to trim it a teeny bit

indicators.note: a bit of the words means only part of their letters, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Some people would like to cut it back just slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'trIM IT A TEeny'.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate is to mimic or reproduce someone else's manner.

clue.text: Peak the day before others

parts.note: eve is the day before an event, as in Christmas Eve
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: Reaching a high point the day before everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest is the highest mountain on Earth, in the Himalayas.

clue.text: A fascinating woman, though a wailer

definitions.meaning: a seductive temptress, from the mythical sea nymphs who lured sailors
a device that gives a loud wailing warning, as on an ambulance

explanation.surface: An alluring woman who is also a crybaby.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a dangerously alluring woman, after Greek myth, and an alarm that howls.

clue.text: He swore it could be quite different

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A man cursed, which might change things.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise means in a different way or state.

clue.text: External changes to rue

indicators.note: changes indicates the letters of the fodder are swapped around

explanation.surface: Someone regrets outside alterations.
explanation.definitionFit: Outer means on the outside, exterior.

clue.text: A measure taken by a sovereign

definitions.meaning: a straight-edged strip for measuring lengths
a monarch or other person who governs

explanation.surface: A king takes action.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a straight measuring stick and one who governs, a monarch.

clue.text: A senseless set-back a censer vationist group finds hard

indicators.note: set back means the word is put in reverse, read backwards

parts.note: mad means senseless, crazy
NT is the National Trust, a British heritage charity

explanation.surface: A heritage charity is unmoved by a foolish reversal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-back' looks like a defeat but turns MAD into DAM. The National Trust preserves historic British houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means unyielding, and also names a legendary unbreakable stone.

clue.text: What's saved a number in harsh surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means the first piece encloses the other

parts.note: savage means harsh or fierce
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Something rescued from a cruel environment.
explanation.walkthrough: L, Roman fifty, goes inside SAVAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvage is property rescued from a wreck or disaster.

clue.text: The man raising a point with a clerical worker

parts.note: E is east, a point of the compass
a rector is a parish clergyman

explanation.surface: A man makes a point to an office clerk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clerical worker' suggests an office clerk, but means a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: An erector is someone who puts up, builds or raises something.

clue.text: Life is real! Life is Longfellow (A Psalm of life)

definitions.text: Life is real! Life is Longfellow (A Psalm of life)

parts.words: Life is real! Life is Longfellow (A Psalm of life)
parts.note: a quotation to complete from Longfellow's poem A Psalm of Life, whose line ends with a word meaning serious or sincere

explanation.surface: A line of Longfellow's poem with its last word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: the poem's line reads 'Life is real! Life is ...', with the blank to be filled.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem's missing word means serious and heartfelt, the mood of the line.
